learn.hook: A kabaddi raider pushes, a magnet pulls a pin without touching it, and a mango falls from the tree. All three are forces, but only one needs a touch!
points: A force is a push or a pull. Its SI unit is the newton (N). A force has both a size (magnitude) and a direction.
A force can start or stop motion, change speed, change direction, or change the shape of an object.
Contact forces act only when objects touch: muscular force (from our muscles), friction, and the push of a spring or a stretched rubber band.
Non-contact forces act from a distance: magnetic force, electrostatic force (a rubbed balloon pulling bits of paper) and gravitational force.
Liquids push upward on objects placed in them. This upward force is called upthrust or buoyant force; it is why a mug feels lighter under water.

example.q: Think it through: You rub a plastic comb on dry hair and bring it near tiny bits of paper. They jump up to the comb. What kind of force is this?
steps: The comb and the paper did not touch before the paper moved.
So it is a non-contact force.
Rubbing gave the comb an electric charge, so it is an electrostatic force.
example.answer: A non-contact force, the electrostatic force.

learn.reallife: A goalkeeper stopping a football, a fridge magnet holding a list and a bucket of water feeling lighter inside a well are all forces in action.

quiz.q: What is the SI unit of force?
quiz.explain: Force is measured in newtons (N), named after Isaac Newton.
steps: Force is measured in a unit named after Isaac Newton
So the SI unit of force is the newton (N)
Answer: Newton
quiz.mistake: Confuses force with mass (kilogram) or pressure (pascal)

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
quiz.explain: A magnet can pull iron without touching it, so magnetic force acts from a distance.
steps: A non-contact force acts without the objects touching
A magnet pulls iron from a distance, so magnetic force is non-contact
Answer: Magnetic force
quiz.mistake: Thinks every force needs touching

quiz.q: A rubbed balloon sticks to a wall. Which force is mainly at work?
quiz.explain: Rubbing charges the balloon, and charged objects attract other objects through the electrostatic force.
steps: Rubbing charges the balloon
Charged objects attract others, so the electrostatic force holds it to the wall
Answer: Electrostatic force
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise electrostatic attraction

quiz.q: Which effect of force is seen when you press a ball of atta dough?
quiz.explain: A force can change the shape of an object, as when dough flattens.
steps: Pressing the dough flattens it
So the force changes its shape
Answer: Its shape changes
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a force can change shape

quiz.q: A mug of water feels lighter when it is still under water in a bucket. Why?
quiz.explain: Water exerts an upward buoyant force, so we need less force to hold the mug.
steps: Water pushes up on objects placed in it
This upthrust (buoyant force) means less force is needed to hold the mug
Answer: Water pushes it upward (upthrust)
quiz.mistake: Thinks gravity disappears under water

quiz.q: Which force pulls a ripe mango down to the ground?
quiz.explain: The Earth's gravity pulls all objects towards it, even without touching them.
steps: The Earth pulls all objects towards it without touching them
So the mango falls because of gravitational force
Answer: Gravitational force
quiz.mistake: Does not identify gravity as the force behind falling

quiz.q: A force always has:
options: Both a size and a direction
quiz.explain: To describe a force fully, we must say how strong it is and in which direction it acts.
steps: A force is described by how strong it is and which way it acts
So a force always has both a size and a direction
Answer: Both a size and a direction
quiz.mistake: Thinks a force has only a size

quiz.q: A batsman hits a ball coming towards him back towards the bowler. The main change in the ball's motion is:
quiz.explain: The bat's force reverses the ball's direction of motion.
steps: The ball was moving towards the batsman and now moves back towards the bowler
The bat's force has changed its direction
Answer: Its direction
quiz.mistake: Does not see that a force can change direction

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: A magnet pulled my metal ring without even touching it! Are there different kinds of forces?
teach.praise: A force is a push or a pull. Some need a touch, like muscle force, and some work from far, like magnets and gravity!
teach.nudge: What is a force? And do all forces need things to touch each other?

revise.summary: A force is a push or pull with size and direction, measured in newtons. It can change motion, speed, direction or shape. Contact forces (muscular, friction, spring) need touching; non-contact forces (magnetic, electrostatic, gravity) act from a distance. Liquids push up (upthrust).
focus: Effects of force: motion, speed, direction, shape
Contact versus non-contact forces with examples
remember: Contact: muscular, friction, spring push; non-contact: magnetic, electrostatic, gravitational
Upthrust makes objects feel lighter in water
traps: A force does not change an object's mass or colour
Gravity and magnetism act without touching, so they are non-contact
Saying only how strong a force is is not enough — give its direction too

learn.hook: Try walking on a freshly mopped marble floor in socks. Whoosh! You slip because there is too little friction under your feet.
points: Friction is a contact force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
Rougher surfaces produce more friction. Pressing the surfaces together harder also increases friction.
Friction is useful: it lets us walk, write, hold things and stop a cycle with brakes. Treads on tyres and soles increase grip.
Friction also wears out shoes and machine parts and produces heat. Lubricants (oil, grease), polishing and ball bearings reduce it.
Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels help. Air and water also oppose motion (drag), so fast vehicles, birds and fish have streamlined shapes.

example.q: Think it through: A heavy box of books is hard to push across the floor. How can you move it more easily?
steps: Sliding friction between the box and floor resists the push.
Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.
So put the box on a trolley with wheels, or on rollers.
example.answer: Use wheels or rollers, so rolling friction (smaller) replaces sliding friction.

learn.reallife: Rubbing your palms together on a cold Shimla morning warms them up. That warmth is the heat produced by friction.

games.title: Friction facts
items: Friction opposes the motion between two surfaces in contact.
That is the definition of friction.
Rolling friction is greater than sliding friction.
Rolling friction is smaller, which is why wheels make moving easier.
Friction can produce heat.
Rubbing surfaces together warms them, like rubbing your hands.
Without friction we could walk more easily.
We need friction between our feet and the ground to walk without slipping.
Streamlined shapes reduce drag in air and water.
Pointed, smooth shapes let air and water flow past easily.

quiz.q: Friction always acts:
options: Opposite to the relative motion between the surfaces
quiz.explain: Friction opposes the sliding or rolling of one surface over another.
steps: Friction resists one surface sliding or rolling over another
So it acts opposite to the relative motion between the surfaces
Answer: Opposite to the relative motion between the surfaces
quiz.mistake: Thinks friction pushes objects forward

quiz.q: Why do tyres have treads?
options: To increase friction and grip on the road
quiz.explain: Treads grip the road better, so vehicles do not skid, especially on wet roads.
steps: Treads grip the road better
They increase friction, so vehicles do not skid, especially on wet roads
Answer: To increase friction and grip on the road
quiz.mistake: Thinks treads are only for decoration

quiz.q: Which reduces friction in the moving parts of a sewing machine?
quiz.explain: Oil is a lubricant. It forms a thin layer that lets parts slide smoothly.
steps: A lubricant forms a thin layer between moving parts
Oil is a lubricant, so it reduces friction in the sewing machine
Answer: Oil
quiz.mistake: Does not know what lubricants do

quiz.q: Why do we slip on a wet, soapy floor?
quiz.explain: The soapy water fills the tiny bumps on the floor, reducing friction between our feet and the floor.
steps: Soapy water fills the tiny bumps on the floor
Friction between feet and floor becomes very small, so we slip
Answer: Friction becomes very small
quiz.mistake: Thinks slipping happens because of more friction

quiz.q: Which is the easiest way to move a heavy gas cylinder across a floor?
options: Push it on a rough mat
quiz.explain: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction. (Gas cylinders should be moved only by adults.)
steps: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction
So rolling the cylinder on its rim is easiest (adults only should move gas cylinders)
Answer: Roll it on its rim
quiz.mistake: Does not know rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction

quiz.q: Why do aeroplanes, fast trains and fish have pointed, smooth shapes?
options: To reduce drag from air or water
quiz.explain: Streamlined shapes let air or water flow around them smoothly, reducing the opposing force.
steps: Air and water oppose motion (drag)
Pointed, smooth (streamlined) shapes reduce this drag
Answer: To reduce drag from air or water
quiz.mistake: Does not link streamlined shapes with fluid friction

quiz.q: What is a disadvantage of friction?
options: It helps us write with a pencil
It wears out shoe soles and machine parts
It lets us hold a glass
It lets brakes stop a cycle
quiz.explain: Rubbing slowly wears away surfaces and wastes energy as heat.
steps: Rubbing slowly wears surfaces and wastes energy as heat
So wearing out soles and machine parts is a disadvantage of friction
Answer: It wears out shoe soles and machine parts
quiz.mistake: Picks a useful effect of friction instead of a harmful one

quiz.q: Which surface gives the most friction to a rolling marble?
quiz.explain: Rough surfaces have more bumps that resist motion, so the marble stops sooner on a doormat.
steps: Rough surfaces have more bumps that resist motion
A rough doormat gives the most friction, so the marble stops soonest there
Answer: Rough doormat
quiz.mistake: Does not link roughness with more friction

teach.ask: Gappu skids on a smooth tile: Wheee! Why did I slide here but not on the rough ground?
teach.praise: Friction opposes motion between surfaces, and rough ground gives more of it than smooth tiles. No more skidding for me!
teach.nudge: What is the force between my feet and the floor called? Does it change on rough and smooth surfaces?

revise.summary: Friction is a contact force opposing relative motion between surfaces; rough surfaces and harder pressing increase it. It helps us walk, write and brake, but wears parts and makes heat. Lubricants and ball bearings reduce it; rolling friction is less than sliding; streamlining cuts drag.
focus: Direction of friction and what increases it
Useful and harmful effects of friction
Ways to reduce friction: lubricants, wheels, ball bearings
remember: Friction opposes relative motion; rougher or harder-pressed surfaces give more friction

learn.hook: An astronaut weighing 600 newtons on Earth would weigh only about 100 newtons on the Moon, yet she would still have exactly the same amount of 'stuff' in her body!
points: Gravity is the force with which the Earth pulls every object towards its centre. Every object with mass attracts others, but the Earth's pull is what we notice.
Mass is the amount of matter in an object. It is measured in kilograms (kg) and stays the same everywhere.
Weight is the force of gravity on an object. Since it is a force, it is measured in newtons (N), using a spring balance.
On Earth, weight (in N) ≈ mass (in kg) × 9.8. So a 1 kg bag of rice weighs about 9.8 N.
The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of the Earth's, so an object weighs about one-sixth as much on the Moon, while its mass does not change.

example.q: Think it through: A watermelon has a mass of 5 kg. What is its weight on Earth (taking 9.8 N for each kg)?
steps: Weight = mass × 9.8

learn.reallife: When ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 lander touched down near the Moon's south pole in 2023, it weighed far less there than on Earth, though its mass was unchanged.

quiz.q: What is weight?
options: The amount of matter in an object
The force of gravity on an object
The speed of a falling object
quiz.explain: Weight is the pull of gravity on an object, so it is a force measured in newtons.
steps: Weight is the pull of gravity on an object
Since it is a force, weight is measured in newtons
Answer: The force of gravity on an object
quiz.mistake: Confuses weight with mass

quiz.q: A school bag has a mass of 4 kg. What is its weight on Earth in newtons (use 9.8 N per kg)?
steps: Weight = mass × 9.8
Answer: 39.2
quiz.explain: Each kilogram is pulled with about 9.8 N, so 4 kg weighs 39.2 N.
quiz.mistake: Thinks weight in newtons is the same number as mass in kg

quiz.q: A box weighs 120 N on Earth. About how much does it weigh on the Moon, in newtons?
steps: Moon's gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's
Answer: 20
quiz.explain: Weight on the Moon is about one-sixth of the weight on Earth.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 6 instead of dividing, or thinks weight does not change

quiz.q: Mira's mass on Earth is 42 kg. What is her mass on the Moon, in kg?
quiz.explain: Mass is the amount of matter in the body, and it does not change from place to place.
steps: Given: mass on Earth = 42 kg
Mass is the amount of matter and does not change from place to place
So the mass on the Moon is still 42 kg; only the weight becomes about one-sixth
Answer: 42
quiz.mistake: Thinks mass changes on the Moon like weight does

quiz.q: Which instrument measures the weight of an object as a force?
quiz.explain: A spring balance stretches according to the pull of gravity on the object and reads it in newtons.
steps: A spring balance stretches according to gravity's pull on the object
It reads the weight in newtons
Answer: Spring balance
quiz.mistake: Does not know which instrument measures force

quiz.q: In which direction does the Earth's gravity pull objects?
quiz.explain: Gravity pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth, which is why things fall 'down'.
steps: Gravity pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth
That is why things fall 'down'
Answer: Towards the Earth's centre
quiz.mistake: Thinks gravity pulls in different directions at random

quiz.q: Why do we weigh less on the Moon than on Earth?
options: There is no air on the Moon
The Moon is closer to the Sun
quiz.explain: The Moon pulls with about one-sixth of Earth's gravity, so weight drops. Mass is unchanged.
steps: The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of the Earth's
So we weigh less there, though our mass is unchanged
Answer: The Moon's gravity is weaker
quiz.mistake: Thinks the absence of air causes lower weight

quiz.q: Which is the correct unit for mass?
quiz.explain: Mass is measured in kilograms. Newton is the unit of force, including weight.
steps: Mass is measured in kilograms
The newton is the unit of force, including weight
Answer: Kilogram
quiz.mistake: Uses 'newton' for mass because it is used for weight

teach.ask: Gappu asks: If I fly to the Moon, will I become smaller? Will I weigh less? I am so confused about mass and weight!
teach.praise: My mass stays the same, but my weight, the pull of gravity, is only about one-sixth on the Moon. Moon trip, here I come!
teach.nudge: What is the difference between mass and weight? And what happens to gravity on the Moon?

revise.summary: Gravity pulls objects towards the Earth's centre. Mass is the amount of matter, in kg, and never changes. Weight is gravity's pull, a force in newtons, measured with a spring balance: weight ≈ mass × 9.8 on Earth. On the Moon weight is about one-sixth, but mass stays the same.
focus: Units: kg for mass, N for weight
Weight on the Moon is about one-sixth
remember: Weight (N) ≈ mass (kg) × 9.8; a 1 kg bag weighs about 9.8 N
Mass stays the same everywhere; weight changes with gravity
traps: Don't divide mass by 6 on the Moon — only weight changes
Weight is in newtons, not kilograms
Gravity pulls towards the Earth's centre, not just 'downward'
